description: Blocking of D2R receiver refers to the interference issue where the D2R receiver may be blocked by a carrier-wave source. This is evaluated under different deployment scenarios: (1) when the carrier-wave source is separately deployed from the D2R receiver (e.g., D1T1-A1 and D1T1-B), relying on spatial isolation; and (2) when the carrier-wave transmitter and D2R receiver are integrated (e.g., D1T1-A2), allowing analog interference cancellation in the RF front-end.

Carrier-wave interference cancellation is a technique used to mitigate interference from a carrier-wave source. It involves spatial isolation, RF interference cancellation, and high-pass filtering. The effectiveness depends on deployment configuration and signal synchronization.

D1T1-A2 is a deployment scenario where the carrier-wave transmitter and D2R receiver are integrated, enabling analog interference cancellation in the RF front-end. This configuration allows for higher interference suppression, especially when a common reference clock is shared between the transmitter and receiver.

D1T1-B is a deployment scenario where the carrier-wave source is separately deployed from the D2R receiver, relying on spatial isolation and interference mitigation techniques such as RF cancellation and high-pass filtering. It supports wired connection between the base station and carrier-wave node, enabling synchronization.
